speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: At the reading of the Massage Establishments Bill in November last year, several Members of Parliament had cautioned that "low-risk activities" that are not required to obtain a massage establishment licence could, nevertheless, be fronts for vice activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Indeed, while open-concept massage establishments operate in full view of the public, they can offer any kind of massage to adult customers.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: This is why even though open-concept massage establishments are exempted from licensing, they have to adhere to a number of conditions.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If they apply, then can they get to operate beyond 10.30 pm?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police will also look at the track record of the operator, whether they have been able to observe, adhere to the conditions that were previously set for them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And, of course, if relevant, the Police will also ask for feedback from the community.
